title: Target-specific regrowth of long axons in the adult mammalian central nervous system

concept.text: The proposed innovation is to repair a severed long-distance pathway in the adult mammalian central nervous system by making surviving projection neurons regrow their axons across an established injury and connect to appropriate downstream targets. Success would require more than fibers extending beyond a lesion: the new connections would need to form functional synapses and carry signals that contribute causally to recovered behavior. The intended capability concerns delayed repair across a chronic lesion, rather than immediate treatment of a fresh cut.

Target specificity has two different meanings that must be kept separate. Reaching the appropriate anatomical region and connecting to the appropriate class of cells would establish an important level of repair. Reconnecting each neuron to its exact original synaptic partners is a stronger claim and would require additional evidence. This record uses appropriate target-class reconnection as the proposed core capability, without assuming that it reconstructs the original wiring in every detail.

The distinction from other routes to recovery is experimentally important. Epidural stimulation and rehabilitation can recruit surviving and remodeled spinal circuitry, while acute fusogenic treatment seeks to repair freshly cut tissue through mechanisms that may include early membrane fusion and later sprouting. Either approach can produce valuable functional improvements without demonstrating target-specific regrowth of long axons across a chronic adult lesion.

significance.text: The revolutionary capability would be biological repair of a disconnected long pathway between surviving circuit elements. The 2022 stimulation study illustrates why this matters: lumbar neurons can survive spinal injury while losing essential commands from the brain, and useful walking can return through recruitment and remodeling of remaining circuitry. Regenerating an interrupted descending pathway would add a distinct route to recovery by rebuilding the damaged connection itself.

Conditional synthesis: if regenerated axons formed appropriate functional synapses, a repaired pathway could support recovery of the skilled functions that depend on it. This would move treatment beyond assisting or reorganizing remaining circuits toward restoring part of the lost anatomical route. The extent of recovery would still depend on whether the originating neurons, downstream targets and other necessary circuit components remained viable.

Conditional applications include repair of pathways involved in movement, sensation or autonomic control, and potentially selected injuries associated with stroke or optic-nerve damage. These possibilities require separate evidence in the relevant pathways and lesion settings. Repair of one named tract would not establish recovery across all these functional systems, nor would an animal demonstration establish safe and effective treatment in humans.

The analogy to salamander-like regeneration is limited. As a conceptual comparison, it captures the ambition to restore damaged neural connections, but it does not establish whole-tissue regeneration, replacement of lost neurons or reconstruction of an entire nervous system. The supplied material also does not substantiate a historical claim that a particular set of master regulators would be sufficient to deliver this capability.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability in the proposed demonstration is coordinated repair: severed axons from surviving adult neurons must grow across a chronic injury, reach appropriate targets, form functional synapses and support useful behavior. The supplied studies do not demonstrate that combination. They support describing mammalian regenerative potential as limited, rather than treating mature neurons as permanently fixed or entirely incapable of growth.

The biological barriers include limited neuronal growth capacity and the degeneration, scarring and other injury-associated processes that impede repair. The reconciled research additionally identifies missing growth substrates, inhibitory myelin and extracellular matrix signals, astrocyte responses and mechanisms within neurons. Those finer mechanistic details were attributed to review articles whose contents were not established in the supplied evidence review; they remain useful candidate explanations rather than independently verified findings within this record.

Engineering synthesis: inducing growth would address only part of the problem. An intervention would also need to control where long axons travel, which cells they contact and whether the resulting connections transmit useful signals. Demonstrating repair requires distinguishing new growth from spared fibers, local sprouting and immediate fusion of cut ends. Lesion crossing alone cannot resolve those alternatives or establish appropriate synaptic targeting.

Proposed translational requirements include delivering growth and guidance interventions to the relevant adult neurons, maintaining their effects over the required distances and duration, and avoiding harmful or inappropriate connections. These are practical requirements inferred from the target capability, not achievements demonstrated by the supplied studies. Human use would require its own delivery, safety and efficacy evidence.

current_state.text: The supplied evidence supports limited mammalian CNS regenerative capacity, but it does not establish the research notes’ stronger developmental claim that regenerative ability is categorically lost during embryonic or early postnatal maturation. The two review articles cited for developmental timing and detailed mechanisms were not substantively assessed in the supplied evidence review. The available findings should therefore be read as a dated account of selected studies, not a comprehensive determination of what the entire field had achieved by November 2026.

In 2022, Kathe and colleagues reported recovery of walking with epidural electrical stimulation and rehabilitation in nine people with chronic spinal cord injury. Walking initially involved robotic support; later outcomes included walking with assistive devices and some recovery without stimulation. These findings establish meaningful functional recovery in the reported participants, without demonstrating target-specific regeneration of an interrupted long tract.

The accompanying mouse experiments reported an injury that completely interrupted corticospinal fibers and substantially depleted descending reticulospinal input. Subsequent walking recovery was associated with remodeling of lumbar circuitry, including increased inputs onto a defined spinal neuron population. Selective inactivation of SC Vsx2::Hoxa10 neurons immediately suppressed stimulation-enabled walking. This supports a causal role for those spinal neurons; it does not establish regeneration of the interrupted corticospinal tract. The supplied text also does not independently substantiate the stronger longitudinal assertion that the tract was shown to remain interrupted throughout recovery.

A PLOS One study published on 10 June 2026 reported functional recovery and axons crossing an injury after immediate PEG-chitosan treatment of freshly transected spinal cords in five three-month-old pigs: three treated animals and two controls. The research notes describe ambulation and lesion-crossing axons at 60 days. These are reported findings in a small juvenile-animal experiment involving an acute treatment bundle, rather than delayed repair across a chronic adult lesion.

The pig study’s described NF-200 staining and retrograde tracing in one animal do not identify the original synaptic targets or establish that recovery depended on regenerated long axons. The authors discuss both early fusion and subsequent sprouting, leaving the mechanism unresolved. The supplied review assessed the complete article text but did not independently inspect its images, so anatomical crossings are appropriately attributed to the authors. This evidentiary limit does not show that the reported crossings or functional improvements were false.

The research notes also attribute a 2024 monkey report to Zhang and colleagues, describing one PEG-treated animal with near-complete hindlimb motor recovery at 18 months and one untreated control that remained paralyzed. The retained PubMed material contained only a cookie notice, so the supplied review could not verify the study identity, methods or numerical account. These details remain an unverified report from the research notes and cannot establish chronic, target-specific regeneration; the access failure is not evidence that the result is false.

Access limitations also constrain interpretation of the 2022 study. Its retained HTML was truncated, although the relevant main text and methods were available to the supplied review. Figures and videos were not inspected, and one supplementary PDF had almost no extractable text. The conclusions above follow the textual evidence described in that review and do not imply independent examination of those visual materials.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: in an adult mammal, interrupt a named long tract by transection or contusion and begin the repair intervention only after a prespecified chronic interval. Establish complete interruption of that tract using imaging together with tract-specific anatomical controls capable of excluding spared fibers. A contusion need not sever the entire spinal cord, but the claimed tract interruption must be demonstrated. These are proposed experimental requirements, not established consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Verified complete tract interruption precedes repair after prespecified chronic delay

completion_criteria.text: Prespecify a substantial fraction of the original projection-neuron population that must regenerate, define how that denominator will be measured and quantify growth beyond the lesion. Anatomical evidence should establish connections onto an appropriate target class, accompanied by physiological evidence of functional synapses. No numerical fraction or chronic interval is established by the supplied evidence. A claim of exact original-partner reconnection would require additional evidence beyond target-class specificity.
completion_criteria.label: Prespecified regeneration fraction forms functional synapses with appropriate target classes

completion_criteria.text: Recovery should occur on a skilled task appropriate to the repaired tract and should depend on the regenerated axons. Selectively silencing those axons, with controls for nonspecific impairment and changes in stimulation or rehabilitation, should abolish or substantially reduce the recovered contribution. The 2022 study supplies an example of selective inactivation testing causal dependence in spinal circuitry; applying that logic specifically to regenerated axons is a proposal here.
completion_criteria.label: Regenerated axon silencing abolishes or substantially reduces skilled-task recovery

completion_criteria.text: Independent replication should reproduce the anatomical, physiological and behavioral findings. Proposed practical boundaries include durable function, assessment of inappropriate connections and adverse effects, and clear reporting of species, age, tract, lesion type and treatment timing. Acute fusion of a fresh cut or stimulation-enabled stepping alone would not meet the proposed bar. Successful finite tests would establish demonstrated breadth within those conditions, without proving regeneration of every CNS pathway or applicability to humans.
completion_criteria.label: Independent replication reproduces functional regeneration with reported practical boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based distinction: NEU-06, Reconstruction of human cognitive circuits after neurons have been lost, addresses rebuilding circuitry after loss of the neurons themselves. NEU-05 instead begins with surviving projection neurons whose axons have been severed. Neuronal replacement could contribute to some larger repair strategies, but neither capability establishes the other, and NEU-06 should not be reduced to a generic neuronal-replacement entry.

Roster-based distinction: NEU-11, Reversible, circuit-specific reopening of critical-period plasticity in the adult brain, concerns renewed capacity for circuit modification. Such plasticity could help integrate regenerated inputs, but it does not itself demonstrate long-axon growth across a lesion. Conversely, axon extension would not establish reversible reopening of a critical period.

Roster-based distinction: NEU-09, Cell-type-specific molecular access throughout the intact adult human brain, could enable delivery of growth or guidance interventions to selected neurons. Its scope is broader than a safe vehicle for growth genes. Molecular access is an enabling capability; it does not establish successful regrowth, target selection or functional repair.

Roster-based overlap: NEU-08, A generative developmental code that builds a specified functional neural circuit, shares the challenge of directing connections toward a functional wiring pattern. NEU-05 concerns repair within an existing adult nervous system rather than specifying and building a circuit through a developmental program. The historical master-regulator and salamander-like regeneration bundle overlaps conceptually only where it includes long-axon regrowth; its provenance and proposed mechanism remain unestablished here.

Roster-based enabling relationships: NEU-02, Routine synaptic-resolution connectomics of entire mammalian brains, could help assess target selection, while NEU-01, Simultaneous spike-resolved recording from every neuron in one behaving mammalian brain, and NEU-03, A prospective theory that predicts mammalian circuit computation from connectivity, could help characterize repaired circuitry. Their full capabilities are not prerequisites for a bounded tract-repair demonstration. None of these measurement or theory advances alone would establish regeneration.

change_log.change: Preserved NEU-05 and its title while defining the core capability as chronic adult long-axon regrowth from surviving neurons to appropriate functional targets.
change_log.reason: Maintains concept identity and separates the proposed innovation from neighboring forms of repair.

change_log.change: Replaced fixed-state and categorical developmental-loss language with limited regenerative capacity, while retaining the finer proposed barriers with an evidence qualification.
change_log.reason: The supplied review supports limited regeneration and injury-associated barriers but did not substantiate the developmental timing or inspect the cited mechanistic reviews.

change_log.change: Separated appropriate target-class reconnection from exact original-partner reconnection.
change_log.reason: Anatomical target-class specificity does not prove restoration of each original synaptic partnership.

change_log.change: Integrated the nine-person 2022 findings, rehabilitation and support conditions, mouse circuit remodeling and selective-inactivation evidence.
change_log.reason: Preserves useful achievements and causal reasoning without equating walking recovery with corticospinal regeneration.

change_log.change: Removed the categorical assertion that the corticospinal tract was demonstrated to remain interrupted throughout recovery.
change_log.reason: The supplied review supports reported initial interruption and later recovery, but not that stronger longitudinal formulation.

change_log.change: Expanded the 2026 pig account with age, sample size, treatment allocation, immediate treatment, reported 60-day outcomes and mechanistic limitations.
change_log.reason: These details distinguish the positive acute-treatment findings from the proposed chronic adult target-specific repair capability.

change_log.change: Retained the monkey report’s 18-month recovery account as explicitly unverified.
change_log.reason: The retained PubMed material was only an access notice; that prevents confirmation without establishing falsity.

change_log.change: Made broader functional and clinical applications conditional and separated them from direct repair of a named tract.
change_log.reason: One pathway demonstration cannot establish recovery of movement, sensation, autonomic function or efficacy across different diseases and species.

change_log.change: Refined completion criteria to include adulthood, chronicity, spared-fiber controls, a defined denominator, functional synapses, causal testing and independent replication.
change_log.reason: These proposed requirements distinguish genuine pathway repair from alternative explanations without presenting arbitrary thresholds as consensus standards.

change_log.change: Corrected neighboring-entry descriptions using the supplied roster and retained historical-regeneration overlap as a qualified conceptual comparison.
change_log.reason: The roster establishes more precise organizational boundaries than the earlier shorthand for NEU-06 and NEU-09.

change_log.change: Preserved source-access and visual-extraction limitations and restricted the field-state conclusion to the supplied dated evidence.
change_log.reason: Partial access and an empty freshness record do not support a comprehensive November 2026 absence claim.

unresolved_issues: The supplied material does not establish whether other contemporary studies demonstrate chronic, target-specific adult CNS axon regeneration; the freshness record is empty.
The developmental timing of reduced regenerative capacity and the detailed mechanisms attributed to the two review articles remain unverified within the supplied evidence review.
The identity, methods and reported 18-month outcomes of the cited monkey study remain unconfirmed because the retained PubMed content contains only an access notice.

The pig study does not resolve the relative contributions of fusion, sprouting and long-axon regeneration, establish original-target reconnection or show causal dependence of recovery on regenerated long axons.
The proposed chronic interval, substantial regeneration fraction, durability requirements and acceptable adverse-effect boundaries require experimental specification.
The historical master-regulator regeneration bundle is not documented sufficiently to establish its provenance or a specific mechanistic relationship to NEU-05.

brief.title: Repairing severed nerve pathways after old injuries
possible: People with an old spinal cord injury could regain lost functions by repairing a severed nerve pathway. Surviving nerve cells would regrow axons, their long signal-carrying fibres, across the injury and reconnect to the right kinds of cells.
why: Rebuilding a lost connection would offer another route to recovery after paralysis. It could restore commands from the brain to surviving spinal circuits and support skilled movement.

sources.showed: Spinal electrical stimulation and rehabilitation restored walking in nine people with longstanding spinal injuries. Mouse experiments identified spinal nerve cells essential to recovery.
sources.quote: This recovery involved a reduction in neuronal activity in the lumbar spinal cord of humans during walking.
sources.cited_for: Surviving spinal circuits can support recovered walking, and selective shutdown can reveal which nerve cells recovery depends on.
sources.not_established: The study did not demonstrate regrowth of a severed long pathway to appropriate targets.

sources.showed: A small monkey study reported near-complete hindlimb recovery after immediate treatment with polyethylene glycol, a substance that can fuse cut membranes. An untreated animal remained paralyzed.
sources.quote: The control animal without PEG remained paralyzed.
sources.cited_for: Immediate treatment of a freshly severed spinal cord was followed by functional recovery in a treated monkey.
sources.not_established: This did not establish delayed repair of an old injury or regrowth to appropriate target cells.

sources.showed: In a small study of young pigs, immediate treatment with a membrane-fusing gel and rehabilitation was followed by walking and reported axons crossing the injury.
sources.quote: Microscopy revealed axons traversing the injury site in the experimental group, whereas control samples showed degenerative post-traumatic changes.
sources.cited_for: Functional recovery and fibres crossing an injury have been reported after immediate treatment of freshly cut spinal cords.
sources.not_established: The study did not distinguish fusion from regrowth or show that appropriately connected new axons caused recovery.

shown: Researchers have recovered walking by recruiting surviving spinal circuits. Separate animal studies report recovery after treating freshly cut spinal cords, with fibres crossing the injury in young pigs.
These results do not yet demonstrate the combined goal: long axons regrowing across an old injury in an adult mammal, connecting to appropriate cells and driving recovered behavior.
missing: Long axons must regrow across an established injury, with surviving fibres and immediate fusion ruled out.
Regrown axons must reach the right cell classes and form synapses, the junctions that transmit signals between nerve cells.
Recovered skilled behavior must depend on those regrown axons.
Independent experiments must establish lasting function and assess harmful or inappropriate connections.

milestones.label: Complete pathway interruption before delayed repair
milestones.explanation: Imaging and pathway-specific anatomical checks would have to establish complete interruption in an adult mammal before treatment after a predefined chronic delay. This would distinguish repair from use of surviving fibres.

milestones.label: Enough regrown axons form working connections with appropriate cells
milestones.explanation: A predefined substantial share of the original nerve-cell population would have to regrow across the injury and form functional synapses with appropriate cell classes. This would establish useful, correctly targeted reconnection.

milestones.label: Switching off regrown axons removes recovered skilled function
milestones.explanation: Selectively silencing regrown axons would have to abolish or sharply reduce recovered skilled performance, with unrelated impairment ruled out. This would show that the repaired pathway causes recovery.

milestones.label: Independent replication establishes reliability and practical limits
milestones.explanation: An independent team would have to reproduce regrowth, functional connections and behavioral recovery, reporting durability, adverse effects and experimental conditions. This would establish reliability and practical limits.

uncertain: The required treatment delay, share of regrowing nerve cells, duration of recovery and acceptable adverse effects still need definition.
The animal results leave unresolved how much recovery comes from membrane fusion, local branching or long-axon regrowth.
Reaching the right cell classes would not establish reconnection to each nerve cell’s exact original partners.

page.title: Target-specific axon regeneration after chronic CNS injury
page.definition: With treatment first begun in a model-defined chronic phase, surviving adult mammalian neurons regrow severed axons, their signal-carrying fibres, across a central nervous system injury to appropriate downstream cell classes. New synapses, junctions between neurons, transmit signals and causally support recovered behavior.

goal.need: Approximately 15.4 million people worldwide were living with spinal cord injury in 2021, accounting for more than 4.5 million years lived with disability that year. Spinal cord injury can cause loss of motor, sensory and autonomic function.

figures.caption: Global burden of spinal cord injury in 2021

figures.note: These estimates cover all spinal cord injuries.

statements.quote: restoring vision through the regeneration of neurons and neural connections in the eye and visual system
statements.context: The 2019 status report records the goal selected in May 2013, with photoreceptors and retinal ganglion cells as its specified targets.

statements.context: The Rehabilitation and Regeneration priority includes interventions for people with spinal cord injury at any stage of life after injury.

completion.title: Regrown adult CNS axons restore behavior through appropriate targets after treatment of chronic injury.
completion.criterion: In an adult mammal, all repair treatment begins after the chronic interval established for the injury model. Identified severed CNS projection axons grow beyond the lesion to their natural downstream target region, form functional synapses on an appropriate neuronal class, and support recovered pathway-dependent behavior. Selective inactivation of the regenerated projection reduces that recovery with controls for nonspecific impairment. Anatomical evidence excludes spared axons and immediate fusion. These findings must coexist in the same injury model.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas synthesis; no outside body located specified this combined test.
completion.basis: Searched NEI AGI reports, DHA SCIRP criteria and published CNS-regeneration protocols; no combined chronic-injury completion test was found. Squair et al. state: “Our causation-testing loss-of-function experiments show that the restoration of function was dependent on the regenerated axons of characterized neurons.” Their growth treatment began 14 days before injury. The chronic optic-tract study reported target reinnervation and pupil responses without selectively inactivating regenerated projections.

milestones.title: Severed adult CNS axons regrow beyond the injury site.
milestones.criterion: Identified cut axons extend beyond the lesion, with spared fibres excluded. Spinal: Cheng and colleagues, published on 8 May 2021, found brainstem respiratory axons beyond a cervical hemisection; anatomical quantification used 7–8 rats per group. Visual: Lim and colleagues, published on 11 July 2016, found short-distance regrowth after 3 weeks of visual stimulation in adult mice, with 5 stimulated animals and 16 controls.
milestones.set_by: The field's convention for canonical axon regeneration, described by Tuszynski and Steward in their 2012 Neuron primer.
milestones.threshold_quote: new growth arising from the cut end of a transected axon, and extending beyond the lesion site

milestones.title: Regenerated adult CNS axons reach their natural downstream target region.
milestones.criterion: Axons traced from an identified injured neuronal population grow past the lesion into that population's normal target region. This establishes regional targeting. Spinal: the study published on 22 September 2023 reported thoracic-to-lumbar regeneration after complete spinal crush injuries; its five behavioral cohorts totalled 30 mice. Visual: the study published on 11 July 2016 found regenerated retinal axons in the superior colliculus, a midbrain visual target, in 6 of 10 adult mice receiving the combined treatment.
milestones.set_by: NEI Audacious Goals Initiative optic-nerve workshop, April 2015, guidance and target-selection criterion. The published requirement concerns retinal axons; the spinal implementation is documented by Squair and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: regenerating axons must find the right target

milestones.title: Regenerated adult CNS axons form functional synapses with appropriate downstream neurons.
milestones.criterion: Regrown axons connect with the appropriate downstream neuronal class and transmit signals to postsynaptic neurons. Visual: the study published on 4 March 2025 combined synaptic anatomy, trans-synaptic tracing and light-evoked responses in the olivary pretectal nucleus; electrophysiology used 6 mice per group after pretreatment. Spinal: the study published on 8 May 2021 found few putative excitatory contacts onto phrenic motor neurons, with contact–function correlation analysis in 7 treated and 8 control rats.
milestones.set_by: NEI Audacious Goals Initiative optic-nerve workshop, April 2015, synapse-formation and circuit-integration requirement, written for retinal axons. Zhang and colleagues provide an electrophysiological implementation.
milestones.threshold_quote: form precise patterns of connectivity with neurons in central visual targets.

milestones.title: Treatment begun in a chronic injury model restores function alongside target reinnervation.
milestones.criterion: Treatment first begins at the chronic interval specified by the published model protocol and produces target-region reinnervation with recovered pathway function. Visual: treatment began 6 weeks after optic-tract injury; the report published on 4 March 2025 described mean pupil constriction of 19% at 7 months in 9 treated mice, versus no response in 5 controls. Spinal: treatment began 8 weeks after cervical hemisection; the report published on 8 May 2021 described limited ventral diaphragm electrical-activity recovery at 24 weeks in 9 treated versus 12 control rats. Re-lesion testing used 4 rats per condition.
milestones.set_by: Zhang and colleagues' 2025 chronic mouse optic-tract protocol and Cheng and colleagues' 2021 chronic rat cervical-hemisection protocol. Their respective 6-week and 8-week intervals are model-specific.
milestones.threshold_quote: To mimic a chronic injury scenario, we initiated this combined treatment 6 weeks after the injury

not_found: No common numerical chronic interval or axon-growth distance was found across the spinal and visual pathway protocols.
The supplied PubMed page for the monkey polyethylene-glycol study could not be read because it returned an access challenge.
